sentences.text: (i) The acquisition of land is for expansion of the Tuticorin Airport.

Originally the requisition body,
namely, the Airport Authority of India proposed to acquire 902 acres of land and subsequently, they modified their proposal of acquisition of land to a lesser extent of 690 acres and finally, in the notification dated 19.08.2010, they proposed to acquire 586 acres.
(j) A Road by name "Theri Road" is running North-South connecting Pudukottai at North and Sawyerpuram at South.
The petitioners' lands are situated very near to this road.
Apart from the said manufacturing units, there are number of industries, farm houses and residential buildings on both sides of the above said road.
The proposed acquisition of the lands for expansion of the Airport de-links the road and thereby the public could not use the road to all in future.

(l) It is to be noted that one VKS Export Industry is functioning in S.No.1 of Servaikaranmadam Village, but the same has been omitted from acquisition on the basis of the Field Inspection Report submitted by the 3rd respondent, wherein the existence of the building of the above industry is mentioned.
The petitioners have also structures and buildings on the lands, which clearly proves the mala fide attitude on the part of the authorities in the matter of selecting lands for acquisition.

(m) Though the authorities have recommended in the field inspection for acquisition of lands to an extent of 1.62.50 Hectares in S.No.1 of the Village, the said Survey Number has been omitted in the Notification.

Instead, the lands in S.No.10/1A1 and 10/1A2 to an extent of 1.51.5 Hectares, which have not been recommended by the authorities, who made the field inspection, have been included in the Notification, which further establishes the improper method adopted by the authorities in the acquisition process.
(n) If the lands in which the manufacturing units are running acquired, the life of the employees will be jeopardized.
Though these facts have been brought to the notice of the authorities, they have not given any consideration.

Under such circumstances, the petitioners challenge the impugned notice dated 02.11.2010 in the present writ petitions stating that the impugned notice was not served upon them in accordance with law.

sentences.text: The present length of Tuticorin Airport is 1350 meters which is sufficient for operation of ATR type aircrafts only.
The Tuticorin Airport is a VFR (Visual Flight Rule) Airport in which the pilot has to handle the aircraft under Visual Flight Rule.
To facilitate the airport for all weather conditions and also for operation of wide body aircrafts, Airports Authority of India has drawn up a master plan for a vision of 20 years.

As per the master plan drawn up, the Airport Authority of India, requisition body requested the State Government for acquisition of 586 acres of land for the expansion and development of Tuticorin Airport.
There is absolutely no mala fide in selection of 586 of acres of lands.
The entire land is required for establishing navigational aids, DVOR, approach lighting system, runway extensions and widening of runway width as per ICAO standards.

The objections of the petitioners were answered by way of remarks by Airports Authority of India stating that due to technical and operational reasons, there is no possibility of change in the master plan.
After considering the objections of the petitioners only, the orders were passed by the acquisition authority on 02.11.2010.
The requisition body received the objections of the petitioners and submitted the remarks on 22.10.2010 well before the final order passed by the acquisition authority.
There is no merit in the writ petitions and as such, the same are liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: District Collector conducted a meeting along with District Revenue Officer and Airport Officials and explaining the purpose of acquisition of lands to all the pattadhars and then received the objection petitions with due care.

Since the District Collector being the District Administration Head was already pre-occupied with other departmental meetings, he directed the District Revenue Officer-cum-Additional District Magistrate to hear the objections and to receive the petitions.

As per the provisions of this Act, the Collector has all powers of delegation and he deputed the District Revenue Officer-cum-Additional District Magistrate to receive and hear objections on his behalf and there is no violation of law.
Hence, the objection petitions received by the District Revenue Officer-cum- Additional District Magistrate are fair and just.
All the objection petitions were sent to the requisition body and after getting remarks, the same were rejected.
The requisition body clearly stated that there is no possibility of changes in the Master Plan and hence, final order was passed by the Collector rejecting all the objections.

9. With regard to the averment made in W.P.No.9004 of 2011 that the land sought to be acquired was given to the petitioner by way of gift by his father and he constructed memorial building for his parents in the proposed land, it is the specific reply of the 2nd respondent that the petitioner has not furnished the exact survey number and village in which the memorial building has been constructed.

No remarks about the memorial building have been furnished in the inspection reports of the 2nd and 3rd respondents on the proposed acquisition of lands, from which it can be inferred that pattadar might have deliberately constructed the memorial building very recently.
Hence, all the writ petitions are liable to be dismissed.

10. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners has submitted that the 2nd respondent made a Notification dated 19.08.2010 in the dailies published on 28.08.2010 under section 3(2) of the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

sentences.text: In the said Notification, the 2nd respondent called for objections from the interested persons within 30 days from the date of publication.
The 30 days' period comes to an end only on 26.09.2010.

But even before the expiry of 30 days, the 3rd respondent had conducted enquiry on A.Ramachandran vs The Secretary To Government on 13 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55649087/

sentences.text: Therefore, the enquiry conducted by the authorities even before the expiry of 30 days for filing objection is without application of mind.
Hence, the impugned order passed by the 2nd respondent is invalid.

11. Learned senior counsel for the petitioners further submitted that as per the provisions of the Act ,
only the Collector has to conduct the enquiry.
But, in the instant case, even according to the 5th respondent, the collector had instructed the 3rd respondent - the District Revenue Officer to conduct the enquiry on 21.09.2010.

In this regard, by inviting the attention of this Court to section 2(a) of the Act, the learned Senior Counsel submitted that "Collector" means the Collector appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Collector under this Act.
But, in the case on hand, absolutely no material to show that the District Revenue Officer - the 3rd respondent has been specifically appointed to perform the duty of the Collector.
Under such circumstances, the non-hearing of the objections by the Collector himself directly is against the provisions of the Act and on that ground also, the impugned order is liable to be quashed.

12. The next fold of submission of the learned senior counsel for the petitioners is that under section 3(2) of the Act, the Government is empowered to issue notice for acquisition of land and under section 23-A of the said Act, the Government may delegate the powers to District Collectors, except certain powers mentioned in the said section, under G.O.Ms.No.513, Revenue (LAI(1), dated 02.09.2005.
Under such circumstances, the Collector alone ought to have conducted the enquiry.
The question of delegating powers further by the District Collector to some other person is not sustainable.
Since the 3rd respondent conducted enquiry in favour of whom the Collector cannot delegate the power, the enquiry conducted by the 3rd respondent is not maintainable.

13. The learned senior counsel for the petitioners further submitted that as per Rule 6(c) of the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Rules, 2001, after filing objections by the pattadhars, the same have to be forwarded to the requisition body, namely, Airports Authority of India and thereafter, after receiving the remarks from the requisition body, necessary order has to be passed by the District Collector by considering the objections as well as the remarks of the requisition body.

sentences.text: But, here, even without getting reply/remarks from the requisition body, the objections were disposed of, which is in violation of said Rule 6(c).
That apart, each objector should be heard individually; but, in the instant case, mass enquiry was conducted.
The learned senior counsel further submitted that no individual notice was sent to the pattadhars, as requied under necessary rule.
Thus, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the entire enquiry is an empty formality.

14. The learned senior counsel for the petitioners submitted that it is the specific case of the petitioner in W.P.No.9004 of 2011 that in the land sought to be acquired, he already constructed a memorial building for his parents and the petitioner is regularly doing pooja in the said memorial;

sentences.text: 15. Learned Additional Advocate General appearing for respondents 1 to 3 submitted that totally 585.98 acres of land was sought to be acquired by the Airport Authority of India.
Out of which, 4.64 acres were poramboke land.
The extent of 581.34 acres of land to be acquired were owned by 1086 persons and only 6 persons were objecting the acquisition proceedings and the Government has received 389 objections.
Out of 586 acres, 33.9 acres alone is in dispute.
These lands were sought to be required for acquisition of Tuticorin Airport.
Acquisition is made only as per the Master plan of the Airport Authority of India.
Therefore, it is incorrect to state that the respondents are adopting pick and choose method in acquiring the lands.

The learned Additional Advocate General, by inviting the attention of this Court to the objections filed by each of the petitioners, has elaborately demonstrated that all the objections were considered properly by the District Collector and thereafter only, the impugned order has been passed.
It is incorrect to state that in W.P.No.9004 of 2011, there has been an memorial in the lands sought to be acquired.

In the inspection report of the Collector, no mention was made to the existence of memorial and if at all any memorial building is in existence in the said land, it should have been constructed only after initiation of acquisition proceedings.

16. With regard to the statement that the enquiry was conducted even before the expiry of 30 days from the date of notice, it is the submission of the learned Additional Advocate General that so far as the present petitioners are concerned, they have submitted all the objections even before the date of enquiry.

The Notification is dated 19.08.2010 itself and the objections were considered only after 30 days; however, the impugned order was passed only on 02.11.2011 after receiving the reply from the acquisition body.
In these circumstances, the petitioners cannot say that the impugned order is invalid since the enquiry has been conducted even before the expiry of 30 days' time given for filing objection.
17. Learned Additional Advocate General further submitted that it is incorrect to state that the enquiry was conducted by the District Revenue Officer.

In fact, at the time of enquiry, the Collector went to the place of enquiry and conducted a meeting with the pattadhars and since the Collector was already pre-occupied with the other official work, he directed the District Revenue Officer to receive the objection petitions and thereafter, the District Collector himself passed the impugned order after considering the reply sent by the requisition body on 02.11.2010.
Under such circumstances, no infirmity could be found in the impugned order passed by the District Collector and, as such, the writ petitions are liable to be dismissed.

19. It is the main submission of the learned senior counsel for the petitioners that the notification under section 3(2) of the Act was published only on 28.08.2010 and as per which, 30 days' time was given to the pattadhars to give objection.
But, before expiry of 30 days, the enquiry was conducted.
Therefore, since the enquiry was conducted before the expiry of 30 days, the entire land acquisition proceedings is vitiated.
By a perusal of the materials available on record, it is seen that there is no dispute that the date of notification was 19.08.2010 and the publication of notification was made only on 28.08.2010.
But, so far as these petitioners are concerned, they have already given their objection before the date of enquiry dated 21.09.2010.

On a perusal of the order dated 02.11.2010 passed by the District Collector, I find that the objections of the petitioners were considered before passing the order by the District Collector - the 2nd respondent herein.

Therefore, at this stage, no infirmity could be found in the enquiry conducted by the 2nd respondent on 21.09.2010.
20.
It is yet another contention of the petitioners that the enquiry was conducted only by the 3rd respondent, who is not a competent person to conduct the enquiry.

In this regard, learned senior counsel has also invited the attention of this Court to section 23-A of the Act and submitted that under section 23-A, delegation was given by the Government only to the District Collector to conduct the enquiry and as per section 2(a) of the Act, "Collector" means the Collector of a District,
and includes any officer specifically appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Collector under this Act.
But, in the instant case, no officer has been specifically appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Collector.
When that being so, the Collector himself ought to have conducted the enquiry, whereas he has conducted the enquiry through the 3rd respondent- District Revenue Officer.

But, a perusal of the materials would show that, as contended by the learned Additional Advocate General, on the date of enquiry i.e.on 21.09.2010, the District Collector himself went to the place of enquiry and he had a brief meeting with the objectors and received objections and thereafter, he instructed the District Revenue Officer to receive the objections since he has to attend other departmental activities and after considering the objections as well as the reply from the requisition body, the Collector has passed the impugned order only on 02.11.2010.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that when the objections and the reply sent by the requisition body were considered by the District Collector before passing the order dated 02.11.2010, now no interference is necessary in the acquisition proceedings merely for the reason that on the date of enquiry after giving brief introduction District Collector left the place of enquiry without receiving the objections.

21. It is yet another submission of the petitioners that as per Rule 6(c), the objections of the pattadhars should be sent to the requisition body and after getting their remarks only, the Collector ought to have passed the order but, in the instant case, it has not been done so.

On going through the materials available on record, I find that on the date of enquiry, 320 objections were received by the District Collector and subsequently, another 69 objections were received till 10.10.2010; all put A.Ramachandran vs The Secretary To Government on 13 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55649087/
10 together, 389 objections were received out of 1086 land owners; all the objections were sent to the requisition body to offer their remarks; the remarks also were received from the requisition body and thereafter only, order has been passed on 02.11.2010.

22. With regard to the contention of the petitioners that the proposed acquisition of the land for expansion of the Airport delinks the "Theri Road"
and, as such, the public would not be in a position to use the road in future, it is to be noted that in the counter filed by the 2nd respondent, it has been specifically stated that the 2nd respondent would advise requisition authority to form a new road to Sayarpuram Panchayat from Pudukottai for the usage of the public or to exclude 80 meters width land from the acquisition proceedings.
In view of the said statement in the counter filed by the 2nd respondent, I do not find any merit in the said contention made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

With regard to the another submission of one of the petitioners in W.P.No.9004 of 2004 that he had constructed a memorial building for his parents, it is to be noted that the District Collector found that there is no such memorial from the inspection report and as such, I am of the view that if at all any memorial is in existence in the said land, as contended by the learned Additional Advocate General, it should have been constructed only after the acquisition proceedings.
23.
Further I find from the materials on record that based on the Master plan submitted by the requisition body, the lands were acquired.

In this regard, it would be appropriate to refer some relevant paragraphs from the counter filed by the 5th respondent - Airports Authority of India in each petition, which are extracted hereunder:
"4. ....the present length of Tuticorin Airport is 1350 meters which is sufficient for operation of ATR type aircrafts only.
The Tuticorin Airport is a VFR Airport in which the pilot has to handle the aircraft under Visual Flight Rule.
The traffic is increasing and there is demand for expansion of facilities including night operations.
To facilitate the airport for all weather conditions and also for operation of wide body aircrafts, Airports Authority of India has drawn up a master plan for a vision of 20 years.
The master plan is drawn as per the requirement of ICAO standards.

As per the master plan drawn up, the Airport Authority of India, requisition body requested the State Government for acquisition of 586 acres of land for the expansion and development of Tuticorin Airport.

As stated earlier request was made to acquire 586 acres of lands as per the master plan drawn up for expansion of Tuticorin Airport......

6. I submit that the Airports Authority of India has drawn up a master plan for Tuticorin Airport for operation of wide body aircrafts such as A.321 type of aircrafts for a vision of 20 years.
An extent of 586 acres is required for expansion of Tuticorin Airport for all weather conditions and also for operation of wide body aircrafts.
The entire land is required for establishing navigational aids, DVOR, approach lighting system, runway extensions and widening of runway width as per ICAO standards.
Further the land is required for construction of new terminal building, passengers amenities and related city side infrastructures.

On taking into consideration of the above facts the Airports Authority of India prepared the master plan and submitted before the State Government and requesting to acquire 586 acres of land for expansion and development of Tuticorin Airport.

As stated earlier, the objections of the petitioner were answered by way of remarks by Airports Authority of India stating that due to technical and operational reasons there is no possibility of change in the master plan.
On taking into consideration of the remarks of the requisition body the acquisition authority rejected the objection of the petitioner.
The remarks pertaining to objections of the petitioner were submitted before the acquisition authority on 22.10.2010 before orders were passed by the acquisition authority on 02.11.2010".

From the said paragraphs, I am of the view that there is no merit in the case of the petitioners that the requisition authorities have adopted a different method to acquire the lands with an object of favouring some interested and influential persons.
On the other hand, I find that the acquisition proceedings are only in accordance with the Master Plan prepared by the Airport Authority of India.

24. Further, the other stand of the petitioners that no individual notice was sent to them is not sustainable in view of the fact that the objectors have already filed their objections before the 2nd respondent.
Further, out of 1086 owners, only six persons were making objection in respect of 33.9 acres alone out of 581.34 acres of land and because of this objection, the entire project came to a stand still.
It is well settled legal proposition that the public interest should prevail over the private interest.
In this regard, it is useful to refer some of the judgments relied on by the learned Additional Advocate General.

In 2011 AIR SC 3210 (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that when a particular project is found to be opposed to the mandate of law or tainted due to mala fide, only in that case the Court can nullify the acquisition of land and not otherwise.

The relevant paragraph reads as follows:
"24.
Here, it will be apposite to mention that NHAI is a professionally managed statutory body having expertise in the field of development and maintenance of National Highways.

The projects involving construction of new highways and widening and development of the existing highways, which are vital for development A.Ramachandran vs The Secretary To Government on 13 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55649087/
12 of infrastructure in the country, are entrusted to experts in the field of highways.

entities.text: A.Ramachandran vs The Secretary To Government
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It comprises of persons having vast knowledge and expertise in the field of highway development and maintenance.
NHAI prepares and implements projects relating to development and maintenance of National Highways after thorough study by experts in different fields.
Detailed project reports are prepared keeping in view the relative factors including intensity of heavy vehicular traffic and larger public interest.
The Courts are not at all equipped to decide upon the viability and feasibility of the particular project and whether the particular alignment would subserve the larger public interest.
In such matters, the scope of judicial review is very limited.
The Court can nullify the acquisition of land and, in rarest of rare cases, the particular project, if it is found to be ex-facie contrary to the mandate of law or tainted due to mala fides.
In the case in hand, neither any violation of mandate of the 1956 Act has been established nor the charge of malice in fact has been proved.

Therefore, the order under challenge cannot be sustained".
25.

In AIR 2005 SC 1 (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:
"22.
In all developed and developing countries there is emphasis on planned development of cities which is sought to be achieved by zoning, planning and regulating building construction activity.

Such planning, though highly complex, is a matter based on scientific research, study and experience leading to rationalization of laws by way of legislative enactments and rules and regulations framed thereunder.
Zoning and planning do result in hardship to individual property owners as their freedom to use their property in the way they like, is subjected to regulation and control.
The private owners are to some extent prevented from making the most profitable use of their property.
But for this reason alone the controlling regulations cannot be termed as arbitrary or unreasonable.
The private interest stands subordinated to the public good.
It can be stated in a way that power to plan development of city and to regulate the building activity therein flows from the police power of the state.

The exercise of such governmental power is justified on account of its being reasonably necessary for the public health, safety, morals or general welfare and ecological considerations; though an unnecessary or unreasonable inter- meddling with the private ownership of the property may not be justified".
26. In 2012 AIR SCW 189 (supra)

, it has been held by the Supreme Court as under:
"7.Ordinarily everywhere in the world wholesale markets are situated at the outskirts or outside the city limits.
No doubt, the shifting of the shops of the wholesellers will cause some hardships to some individuals, but it is well settled that public interest prevails over the private interests.

Thus, in Friends Colony Development Committee vs. State of Orissa AIR 2005 SC 1 (vide para 22) this Court observed :
"The private interest stands subordinated to the public good.".

sentences.text: 13. It must be remembered that certain matters are by their very nature such as had better be left to the administrative authorities instead of Courts themselves seeking to substitute their own views and perceptions as to what is the best solution to the problem.
The present is clearly an instance where this Court should not interfere with the steps taken by the respondents to resolve a pressing problem.
In matters of policy the Courts have a limited role and it should only interfere with the same when it is clearly illegal.
That clearly is not the case here.
The impugned action is a salutary step for undoing a mischief, which was crying out for redress for a long time, and it is not illegal."
27. In 2012 (4) SCALE 602, it has been held by the Supreme Court that the public welfare should prevail as the highest law and private interest would stand subordinate to public good.
The relevant paragraphs are extracted hereunder:

19. The legislative intent attaching due significance to the 'public safety' is evident from the object and reasons of the Act, the provisions of the Act and more particularly, the Rules framed thereunder.

Even if we assume, for the sake of argument, that Rule 100 is capable of any interpretation, then this Court should give it an interpretation which would serve the legislative intent and the object of framing such rules, in preference to one which would frustrate the very purpose of enacting the Rules as well as undermining the public safety and interest.
Use of these black films have been proved to be criminal's paradise and a social evil.

The petitioner has rightly brought on record the unanimous view of various police authorities right from the States of Calcutta, Tamil Nadu and Delhi to the Ministry of Home Affairs that use of black films on vehicles has jeopardized the security and safety interests of the State and public at large.

This certainly helps the criminals to escape from the eyes of the police and aids in commission of heinous crimes like sexual assault on women,
robberies, kidnapping, etc.
If these crimes can be reduced by enforcing the prohibition of law, it would further the cause of Rule of Law and Public Interest as well.

20. This Court in the case of Hira Tikoo v. Union Territory of Chandigarh [(2004) 6 SCC 765], while dealing with the provisions of town planning and the land allotted to the allottees, upon which the allotees had made full payment, held that such allotment was found to be contravening other statutory provisions and the allotted area was situated under the reserved forest land and land in periphery of 900 meters of Air Force Base.

sentences.text: The Court held that there was no vested right and public welfare should prevail as the highest law.

Thus, this Court, while relying upon the maxim "salus populi est suprema lex", modified the order of the High Court holding that the allottees had no vested right and the land forming part of the forest area could not be taken away for other purposes.

Reference can also be made to the judgment of this Court in Friends Colony Development Committee v. State of Orissa [AIR 2005 SC 1], where this Court, while referring to construction A.Ramachandran vs The Secretary To Government on 13 March, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55649087/
14 activity violative of the regulations and control orders, held that the regulations made under Orissa Development Authorities Act, 1982 may meddle with private rights but still they cannot be termed arbitrary or unreasonable.

21. In the present case as well, even if some individual interests are likely to suffer, such individual or private interests must give into the larger public interest.
It is the duty of all citizens to comply with the law.
The Rules are mandatory and nobody has the authority in law to mould these rules for the purposes of convenience or luxury and certainly not for crime.

We may also note that a Bench of this Court, vide its Order dated 15th December, 1998 in Civil Appeal No. 3700 of 1999 titled Chandigarh Administration and Others v. Namit Kumar & Ors., had permitted the use of 'light coloured tinted glasses' only while specifically disapproving use of films on the vehicles.

sentences.text: Subsequently, in the same case, but on a different date, another Bench of this Court vide its order reported at [(2004) 8 SCC 446] made a direction that mandate of sub-Rule (2) of Rule 100 shall be kept in mind while dealing with such cases."

28. The principles enunciated in the above judgments would clearly show that public welfare is the highest law and even if some individual interests are likely to suffer, such individual or private interests must give up in the larger public interest.

So far as the present petitions are concerned, it is pertinent to note that out of 1086 persons, 1080 owners had accepted the land acquisition proceedings and only six owners were objecting, that too without any valid reasons.

Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the District Collector had conducted the enquiry in proper manner and passed the impugned order only in accordance with the provisions of the Act and as such, all the writ petitions are liable to be dismissed.
In the light of what is stated above
, I do not find any valid ground to make interference.
Hence, all the writ petitions are dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected M.Ps.are closed.
